_about: SCRIPTED FAKE MEETING (not a real recording). A 3-minute Q3 revenue review with four speakers. Replayed through the real backend by scripts/replay.py as Recall-shaped webhooks. Times are seconds from the start of the call.
title: Q3 revenue review (fake meeting)

lines.text: Okay, let's get started with the quarterly revenue review.
Thanks Tom. I'll walk through the headline numbers first, then Marcus can cover pipeline.
Total bookings for the quarter came in at fifty two million.
That's slightly ahead of plan, right?
About two percent ahead, yes.
The enterprise segment drove most of that, especially the two renewals in September.
Churn stayed flat at around three percent, which is in line with the model.
And honestly the momentum is great. Q3 revenue was rising, up about three percent on Q2.
Hmm, I'm not sure that's right, I remember it being lower.
Let's not get stuck on it, we can check after.
Moving on, gross margin improved to sixty one percent.
What drove the margin improvement?
Mostly lower hosting costs after the migration.
Quick side note, the bot we added answers when you say hey AGI, so be careful.
Good to know.
Hey AGI, what was Q3 revenue according to the board deck?
Okay, so it actually fell. Dana, can you reconcile that with the bookings number?
Yes, bookings lead revenue by a quarter, so the dip reflects Q2 bookings.
Fair enough, my mistake on the direction.
Marcus, what does the Q4 pipeline look like?
Pipeline is about ninety million, with thirty million in late stage.
I'll update the forecast model with the new late-stage numbers by Friday.
Great. Dana, please send the reconciled revenue bridge to the board.
Will do.
Thanks everyone, let's wrap up.

planted.contradiction_note: Marcus says Q3 revenue was rising; knowledge/SAMPLE_board_deck_q3.md says it fell 4%. Priya's doubt (line 8) is the uncertainty signal.
planted.wake_mention_note: Talks ABOUT the wake word - must NOT trigger speech mode.
